headline: Your own long-form went up today, “Did Hindus Kings Loot Temples?”: fix “Hindus” to “Hindu” in the title now and judge it on 30 November. The Churchill Short has to be written today to be recorded tomorrow, and at its recent pace the Indonesia long-form is days from becoming the channel's fifth breakout.

top3.signal: Bentinck's regulation against sati in Bengal is seven days out, and your Short “The Year Britain Banned Sati, Englishmen Were Selling Their Wives” is written and sourced, not recorded.
top3.recommendation: It takes the Tegh Bahadur slot tomorrow. Record by 2 December and publish the morning of 4 December, with “Sati” in the title because that is what people search. First settle the line the script itself flags: “never wrote a law” needs checking, since courts acted on wife sales under other charges. The Ayodhya inscription Short, written on 1 November, follows on the morning of 6 December.

top3.topic: 14 December 1971: the killing of Bengal's intellectuals
top3.signal: Seventeen days out, two days before Vijay Diwas. The research step falls on 30 November.
top3.recommendation: From 30 November, find who drew up the list and who carried it out, with names and the date. Script a Short for the morning of 14 December with the culprit in sentence one, about two minutes long to bring subscribers, judged on day three.

top3.signal: Twenty days out; the research step falls on 3 December. The same date marks the Saunders killing by Bhagat Singh and his comrades.
top3.recommendation: From 3 December, check what Timur's own memoir says about the prisoners killed before the battle, and whether historians accept the memoir. If it holds, a Short for the morning of 17 December that opens on his own words. The channel's earlier Timur Short brought no subscribers, so this is a guess. Skip the Saunders date: freedom-fighter biographies are the channel's weakest Shorts.

skipped.signal: Constitution of India readership is 2.73x its usual in Hindi, and #ConstitutionDay led India's X trends.
skipped.recommendation: Skip. The day has passed, and the channel's Short on it, “Why Is Lord Rama in the Original Constitution of India?”, brought no subscribers (0 per 1,000).

whats_working: “How the Ramayana Was REWRITTEN to Convert Hindus” is the best subscriber-earner of this month's uploads: 3.8 net per 1,000 views on 123,006 views, and it pushed long-form views up 102.4% week over week. Over 28 days long-form earns 87.0% of the net subscribers videos bring.

The 90-day window's best converter is still “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History”, 12.7 net per 1,000 views: a named historian convicted by his own record. Today's long-form has the same shape, a named historian checked against the inscriptions.

Searchable names keep earning: “Why Is Ram Setu Called ADAM'S Bridge?” has 12,765 views and still draws a few hundred a day three weeks on, largely from people searching “ram setu” and “adams bridge”. The Churchill Short needs his name first in the title for the same reason.
whats_wrong: Viewers leave the Indonesia long-form early: average view is 27.8%, and 16 points of the audience go at 0:19. The transcript is in now and shows why: at 0:19 the script leaves its hook, the Malay Ramayana in which Ravana gets his powers from Allah, for what Indians already forward about Indonesia (“In India we love to share that its currency once featured Ganesha”). The channel's own lesson from the India Ramayana video: “When the hook names a conflict, the next sentence must stay inside it.” Test: the Bali script stays inside its opening act for the first 30 seconds.

Long-form views overstate real viewing: only 41.6% of November's long-form views were engaged views, and over the 365-day window long-form now brings 7.1 subscribers per 1,000 views, below its usual range. The Asia Ramayana video brings 2 per 1,000 and the India one 1.2. Probable cause: Home-feed plays that are not real viewing. Test: judge today's long-form on 30 November by engaged views and subscribers, not by views.

Shorts views fell 83.6% week over week (20,652 against 126,126) as the film Shorts aged. The newest, “Why Portuguese Goa Taxed Every Hindu's SHIKHA”, has 1,572 views and no subscribers yet; it loses viewers at 0:05 and again at 0:09, where the blame moves from the Portuguese to Aurangzeb (“The Portuguese were inspired by Aurangzeb”). Probable cause: two culprits in the first 10 seconds. Test: the Churchill and Sati Shorts keep one culprit through the first 15 seconds.

The three Halley Kalyan clips that went up in the same minute on 3 November have 24, 97 and 264 views. Probable cause: three clips from one conversation competing with each other, each opening on talk rather than on something that happened. Test: the next interview clip goes out alone, a day clear of any other Short, opening on a dated fact.

actions.action: Fix the title of today's long-form: “Did Hindus Kings Loot Temples?” should read “Did Hindu Kings Loot Temples?”.
actions.rationale: It has 20 views so far, so almost nobody has seen the misspelling yet, and “hindu kings” is what a searcher would type. Fix it before Home and search start testing it widely.

actions.action: Upload the Malay Ravana Short: title starting “Ravana”, Related video set to the Indonesia long-form, its link in the pinned comment, and the Malay “Hikayat Seri Rama” named on screen.
actions.rationale: Written since 19 November to send viewers to the Indonesia long-form, which still brings subscribers every day but fewer than in its first week. Whether a Short sends viewers on is a guess.

actions.action: Answer the fact-check and the Indonesian viewer's correction under the Indonesia video with sources (/replies drafts them), and pin a correction if a point is wrong.
actions.rationale: The Bali video goes to the same viewers; a fix made before it protects it.

growth.verdict: Needs 224 net subscribers a day. The channel does 70.27/day, so the target is a **3.2x** change in rate. Every lever this channel has demonstrated, pulled at once (scenario "1. Current rate, nothing changes"), reaches 70.3/day — still 3.2x short. At that ceiling rate 100,000 arrives on 2030-02-01, 3.2 years out.

scenarios.name: 1. Current rate, nothing changes
assumptions: Measured: channel_totals_daily, everything the channel publishes, last 28 days.
Same formats, same cadence, same lane mix.
Includes the channel's one breakout: "Chakla: How the British Raj Created a ‘Licensed Vice’ System" is 1282 of the 3,328 subscribers that 22 fresh long-form videos produced.

scenarios.name: 2. Stop Shorts, same effort into long-form (no breakout)
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 31.8/day (890 of 1,827 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Measured: 22 long-form and 106 Shorts published in the last 365 days.
ASSUMPTION (not measured): 6 Shorts cost what 1 long-form costs, so the Shorts become 17.7 more long-form videos a year — 39.7 in total.
Measured: MEDIAN 33 subscribers per fresh long-form video. The mean is 151, inflated by one breakout, so the median is the honest number for planned output.
Gives up the 452 subscribers a year the Shorts brought in; they are simply absent from this total.
Below scenario 1 because scenario 1 contains a breakout and this one does not. That is the point, not an error.

scenarios.name: 3. All long-form, all revision lane (no breakout)
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 31.8/day (890 of 1,827 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Scenario 2's cadence, every topic chosen from the revision lane.
Measured on the same fresh set: 9 revision long-form videos, median 69 subscribers, against 33 for fresh long-form overall.
ASSUMPTION: the lane median holds as output scales. It rests on a small number of videos and is the weakest link here.

scenarios.name: 4. Scenario 3 plus one breakout a quarter
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 31.8/day (890 of 1,827 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Scenario 3, plus four videos a year performing like the best video the channel has ever published.
Measured: "Chakla: How the British Raj Created a ‘Licensed Vice’ System" brought 1,282 subscribers on 73,159 views.
ASSUMPTION: a breakout that size can be produced to order, four times a year. The channel has produced one.
